title: Coefficient restriction detects geometric-fibre endomorphisms
statement: Fix a prime l, a Noetherian separated scheme Y on which l is invertible, a geometric point y, and an algebraic closure K of Q_l. Use the rational sheaf categories, rational fibres and coefficient diagram of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. For each finite intermediate field E choose any functor S_E to E-modules whose object values are those rational fibres and whose maps satisfy the pure-tensor formula of [lem-pod-lisse-rational-scalar-fiber-comparison]. Transport S_E followed by extension E→K to the recorded category P(E), obtaining J_E. Then for each E, precomposition along P(B→E), where B is the least coefficient field of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], is a bijection from natural endomorphisms of J_E to natural endomorphisms of P(B→E) followed by J_E.

source.place: Weil II (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147, restriction and extension of coefficients; literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite separable case

proof.text: Restrict each integral E-level to the integers of B, taking level e(n+1)-1 for ramification index e. Its annihilation and transition kernels are the B-uniformizer powers because the mapped ideal is the e-th power of the E-uniformizer ideal. Finite coefficient quotients make the stalks finite sets and hence finite B-integer modules; local constancy is preserved. Cofinality identifies its integral fibre with the restricted integral fibre. Rationalize maps by clearing denominators with powers of the B-uniformizer; the pure-tensor formula identifies their rational fibres. Commensurable lattices give isomorphic rational restrictions.

First use the proved rational scalar comparison and the diagram category and arrow equalities to identify P(B-to-E) followed by J_E with J_B, and conjugate the given endomorphism. Apply the resulting B-fibre endomorphism to the restriction of each E-sheaf. Naturality for multiplication by E makes it E-equivariant. The separability idempotent selecting the inclusion E→K in K tensor_B E defines its restriction to the prescribed E-fibre: a primitive element and the coprime factorization of its separable minimal polynomial construct that idempotent by the Chinese remainder theorem. Morphisms commute with this idempotent, giving naturality. On a sheaf extended from B, its restriction is a finite direct sum; naturality for its inclusions and projections shows the extension returns the original endomorphism.

Each E-sheaf is a retract of the E-extension of its B-restriction, by the diagonal idempotent in E tensor_B E. Naturality for the retraction proves uniqueness. Transport through the diagram obj_eq and map_eq to obtain precisely the displayed whiskering bijection.

theorem lisseCoefficientFiberEndomorphisms_whisker_bijective
    (S : ∀ E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l K,
      LisseRationalSheaf l E₀.val Y ⥤ ModuleCat.{d + 1} E₀.val)
    (hS : ∀ (E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l K)
      (F : LisseRationalSheaf l E₀.val Y), (S E₀).obj F = lisseRationalFiber l E₀.val Y y F)
    (hmap : ∀ E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l K,
      IsLisseRationalFiberFunctor Y y l E₀.val (S E₀) (hS E₀)) :
    let P := (lisseCoefficientDiagramData l Y K).diagram
    let J := fun E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l K ↦
      (eqToHom ((lisseCoefficientDiagramData l Y K).obj_eq E₀)).toFunctor ⋙
        S E₀ ⋙ ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap E₀.val K)
    ∀ E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l K,
      Function.Bijective (fun u : J E₀ ⟶ J E₀ ↦
        Functor.whiskerLeft (P.map (homOfLE
          (show Padic.finiteCoefficientBase l K ≤ E₀ from
            show (⊥ : IntermediateField ℚ_[l] K) ≤ E₀.val from bot_le)).toLoc).toFunctor u)
